issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the fingerprint size from 2048 to 4096 bits and switches from bit fingerprints to count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). It uses no file or network access, no pasted answers and no test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Count fingerprints feed a random forest normally. A 1624x4096 float32 matrix needs about 27 MB, well inside the memory limit, and the runtime cost should be small.

My z: candidate mean (0.0994 + 0.0957) / 2 = 0.09755. Incumbent mean 0.1069. Difference 0.00935. Standard error 0.0049 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00600. That gives z ≈ 1.56, close to the reported 1.565. The small gap is probably rounding in the inputs.

The evidence is weak. z ≈ 1.56 is below the usual threshold of 2, and the incumbent has only one run, so its mean is itself noisy (sd about 0.0049). The accept is provisional; a replicate run of the incumbent or candidate would make it more reliable.
The diff makes two changes at once (4096 bits and count fingerprints), so the gain can't be credited to either one. This is not a validity problem.
